title: Military Working Dog Handler (MSgt to Pvt) NMOS (5811), DC I&L
raw_text:
3.     MOS 5812, Military Working Dog Handler (MSgt to Pvt) NMOS (5811), DC I&L

    a. Summary. A Military Working Dog Handler is a military policeman who
is additionally trained to employ a military working dog, with on or off-



                                        3-330                        Enclosure (1)
 3136                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



leash directional control, in order to conduct searches of open areas,
buildings, vehicles, and roadways, detect explosives or illegal drugs, locate
missing personnel by tracking or scouting, and detect and/or apprehend lost
or wanted personnel, and intruders.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a volunteer.

            (2) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811.

        (3) To protect against certain infections from dogs, handlers must
have a spleen.

        (4) Military working dog handlers seeking an instructor assignment to
Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA)-Lackland must possess an associate’s degree or
have the ability to complete the required associate’s degree within the
prescribed time from date of assignment. Upon assignment, instructors who do
not meet the requirement will develop an associate degree plan through the
education service office. This education requirement is the standard
criteria for an instructor assigned to any Air Force owned courses, Community
College of the Air Force (CCAF), as described in reference (dp), the most
current version of the memorandum of agreement between each service branch’s
training command.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Military Working Dog Basic Handler’s
Course (F06MTM1) Joint Base San-Antonio-Lackland, TX.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers 33-3051.

       f.   Related Military Skill.    None.

CORRECTIONS 1. Introduction. The Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections OccFld provides the installation commander continuous support by enforcing the law, preventing and suppressing crime, assessing command physical security posture, preserving military control, quelling disturbances, investigating offenses, apprehending offenders, protecting property and personnel, investigating traffic accidents, controlling traffic, providing first response to active shooters incidents and special response to a barricaded subject, guarding military prisoners and supervising brig operations and correctional custody units. Provide the MARFORRES Commander support to security and mobility operations, battlefield circulation and traffic control, rear area security operations to include limited offensive and defensive combat operations, detention operations to include handling and safeguarding prisoners of war, refugees, or evacuees, guarding military prisoners, and returning absentees/deserters to military control.

3. MOS 5812, Military Working Dog Handler (MSgt to Pvt) NMOS (5811), DC I&L a. Summary. A Military Working Dog Handler is a military policeman who is additionally trained to employ a military working dog, with on or off- leash directional control, in order to conduct searches of open areas, buildings, vehicles, and roadways, detect explosives or illegal drugs, locate missing personnel by tracking or scouting, and detect and/or apprehend lost or wanted personnel, and intruders. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a volunteer. (2) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811. (3) To protect against certain infections from dogs, handlers must have a spleen. (4) Military working dog handlers seeking an instructor assignment to Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA)-Lackland must possess an associate’s degree or have the ability to complete the required associate’s degree within the prescribed time from date of assignment. Upon assignment, instructors who do not meet the requirement will develop an associate degree plan through the education service office. This education requirement is the standard criteria for an instructor assigned to any Air Force owned courses, Community College of the Air Force (CCAF), as described in reference (dp), the most current version of the memorandum of agreement between each service branch’s training command. c. Requirements. Complete the Military Working Dog Basic Handler’s Course (F06MTM1) Joint Base San-Antonio-Lackland, TX. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
